description.narrative: EmPower: Kvinnor för ett klimatresilient samhälle fas II är ett samarbetsprojekt mellan UN Women och UNEP med fokus på jämställdhet, klimatanpassning, katastrofriskreducering och förnybar energi. Projektet kommer att ha ett regionalt fokus på Asien och Oceanien, men kommer även ha verksamhet i Bangladesh, Kambodja, Vietnam, Indonesien och Filippinerna.

EmPower: Women for Climate-Resilient Societies Phase II is a joint project between UN Women and UNEP focusing on gender, climate change adaptation, disaster risk reduction and renewable energy.The project will have a regional focus on Asia and the Pacific but will also have operations on the ground in Bangladesh, Cambodia, Viet Nam, Indonesia and the Philippines.

Overall Impact: People in Asia Pacific are less vulnerable to the impacts of climate change and experience greater gender equality and the full enjoyment of their rights, including equal access to a clean, healthy and sustainable environment. More specifically, the proposed project will contribute to three outcomes:
Outcome 1: Asia Pacific actors increase action on gender responsive climate change adaptation and mitigation.
Outcome 2: Women in all their diversity and other marginalized groups are represented as key environmental actors in climate and DRR decision making.
Outcome 3: Women and other marginalized groups in Asia Pacific secure climate resilient livelihoods
The programme will move forward with implementation not only in Bangladesh, Vietnam and Cambodia, but has also expanded to Indonesia and the Philippines with the additional funds from the new donors. The programme will also have more focus on the regional level than in the first phase. This includes collaborating with regional organisations such as the ASEAN Secretariat, The South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC), the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD), as well as the Secretariat of the Pacific Regional Environment Programme (SPREP), and by sharing learning and experience broader within the Asia Pacific region.

description.narrative:
The programme implementation under all three outcomes was reported to be on track, demonstrating strong country and regional progress and enhanced collaboration across government, civil society, and financial institutions. Country highlights showcased concrete policy shifts, support to resilient livelihoods through entrepreneurship, and innovative communication efforts advancing womens leadership in climate action.
At the national level, ongoing normative support is catalysing policy and institutional support through strengthening policies and government institutions. In Bangladesh, the programme is supporting the operationalization of the Climate Change Gender Action Plan (ccGAP) in collaboration with Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) and Ministry of Women and Children Affairs (MoWCA), extending gender-responsive action planning to seven additional ministries and engaging 100 CSOs in developing Local Adaptation Plans (LAPAs) across five upazilas. These efforts embedded gender priorities in national and local planning and budgeting processes. In the Philippines, collaboration with the Climate Change Commission and the Philippine Commission on Women is strengthening the Peoples Survival Fund (PSF) by integrating gender dimensions into its handbook and GAD guidelines, unlocking a 1 billion annual adaptation fund for local governments. Cambodia conducted its first national Gender and Environment Survey through the collaboration between EmPower and the Women Count programme, creating a baseline for genderenvironment indicators now informing NDC 3.0 updates and local climate and DRR plans.
At the regional level, UN Womens and UNEPs leadership in the ASEAN Climate Change Strategic Action Plan (ACCSAP) placed gender and social inclusion at the forefront of regional climate frameworks. Technical workshops by UN Women with BIMSTEC and ICIMOD advanced regional knowledge exchange on gender-responsive climate action, while partnerships with SPREP in the Pacific supported womens participation in NDC revision processes and climate decision-making.
